# Selected technical work

This page brings together scientific publications and software projects. Project descriptions distinguish verified implementation details from capabilities that still need validation.

## Scientific publications

### Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion (2008)

**Jean-Marc Brun and Bijan Mohammadi**  
Book chapter in *Partial Differential Equations: Modelling and Numerical Simulation*, pp. 245–256.

The chapter presents reduced-complexity modelling for passive-scalar transport and environmental dispersion. The work uses similarity-based modelling to estimate concentrations without solving a full spatial PDE over the entire domain.

- [Chapter record — Springer](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14)
- [Book record — Springer](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5)

### Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite (2006)

**Bijan Mohammadi and Jean-Marc Brun**  
*Comptes Rendus. Mécanique*, 334(10), 634–638. DOI: 10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007.

This paper presents a reduced-complexity approach to passive-scalar transport and dispersion. It develops similarity solutions in a non-symmetric metric based on transport times and uses partial observational data for model identification.

- [Publisher record and abstract — Comptes Rendus. Mécanique](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/)
- [Alternative bibliographic record — Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Similitude-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ralis%C3%A9e-et-mod%C3%A9lisation-g%C3%A9om%C3%A9trique-Mohammadi-Brun/16f7bdf72d12165abf39078f4078438162304fbe)

These publications document research on reduced-order modelling and environmental dispersion. The publisher records are the primary references.

### Contribution mentioned in a public-health exposure report (2006)

**Évaluation de l’exposition aérienne aux pesticides de la population générale — Étude en air extérieur dans quatre sites de l’Hérault en 2006**

The report examines pesticide concentrations in outdoor air at four sites in Hérault and discusses population exposure. Jean-Marc Brun is listed among people who also participated in the study; the report does not specify his individual role or contribution.

## Wiki Knowledge — persistent, source-grounded knowledge base

**Goal**

Build a maintainable personal knowledge base from documentary sources, with Markdown pages, metadata, cross-links, and source traceability.

**Implementation visible in the repository**

- Python package with a CLI and modular engines for ingestion, search, validation, linting, synchronisation, and export
- Markdown pages and YAML configuration/front matter
- Pydantic-based data models and structured search results
- Lexical retrieval using BM25 and TF-IDF
- A Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) path for combining ranked results
- GitHub Actions workflows intended to automate source ingestion and related maintenance

**Engineering focus**

The project explores how to turn LLM-assisted document processing into a maintainable engineering workflow: structured outputs, traceability, validation, and explicit maintenance operations rather than relying on one-off chat responses.

**Current limitations to resolve**

The current search implementation's vector-search method falls back to the BM25 path; it should not yet be described as a functioning embedding-based semantic search system. The README and some automation workflows also appear out of sync with the package layout and declared Python requirements. These are tracked as engineering follow-up work, and the repository's checks should be run before relying on every documented workflow.

**Repository and documentation**

- [Wiki Knowledge source code](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge)
- [README and architecture overview](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge#readme)
- [Open issues and engineering follow-up](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge/issues)

## LLM hallucination evaluation benchmark

**Goal**

Compare approaches to detecting unsupported or hallucinated content in language-model outputs using an evaluation protocol that makes comparisons interpretable.

**Technical work**

- Integration of multiple fact-checking and evaluation systems
- Metric calculation and aggregation from predictions
- Threshold analysis and trade-offs between metrics
- Streamlit visualisation of benchmark results and errors
- Modular code and tests for calculation components

**What it demonstrates**

Evaluation engineering: defining labels and units of analysis, checking metric validity, and distinguishing supported conclusions from claims the data cannot justify.

**Repository status**

A public repository URL, shareable datasets, full protocol, and numerical results have not yet been verified. No repository link or benchmark result is claimed here.

## Attribution and evidence

Scientific publications above link to publisher records that identify Jean-Marc Brun as an author. The public-health report is described only as a report that lists him among participants, not as an authored publication. Other supplied sources concerning atmospheric dispersion or pesticide spray drift are not listed as personal publications because the available metadata identifies other authors.

Software descriptions are based on the public repository documentation and inspected source files. Capabilities that are incomplete or not yet validated are identified as limitations rather than presented as completed features.
